card.title: Track the Cost That Returns
card.instruction: Accept every twist, but keep returning to one practical consequence whose importance grows as the scene becomes more complicated.

transfer.action: I bring the original overflowing bucket beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: Every new twist still drips in here. {request}
transfer.response: Right. The same leak is filling the bucket faster. {counter}
transfer.closing: All right. Does it stop the water, or do we need another bucket while we deal with it?

originalTransfer.action: I bring the original overflowing bucket beside {prop}.
originalTransfer.opening: Every new twist still drips in here. {request}
originalTransfer.response: We're still paying for the first loose screw. {counter}
originalTransfer.closing: Does it empty the bucket or only give us another thing to announce above it?

card.title: Track the Cost That Returns
card.instruction: Accept every twist, but keep returning to one practical consequence whose importance grows as the scene becomes more complicated.

originalDialogue.speaker: A
originalDialogue.text: Fine, the fountain grants wishes. Who pays its water bill?

originalDialogue.speaker: B
originalDialogue.text: It can wish the water free.

originalDialogue.speaker: A
originalDialogue.text: Then who pays the sewer charge?

originalDialogue.speaker: B
originalDialogue.text: It has turned the pipes to gold.

originalDialogue.speaker: A
originalDialogue.text: Lovely. Does the same meter now charge us for gold drainage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our garden fountain grants wishes. Fine. We're still paying for its water.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wished for ten more. We can sell admission.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Eleven fountains on our meter. Charge enough to cover that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Visitors wished for fountains at home. They're all fed from ours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we're paying to water the whole queue's gardens. Sell them monthly passes before the next bill arrives.

card.title: Track the Cost That Returns
card.instruction: Accept every twist, but keep returning to one practical consequence whose importance grows as the scene becomes more complicated.

originalDialogue.speaker: A
originalDialogue.text: I accept that the house travels through time. The roof still leaks.

originalDialogue.speaker: A
originalDialogue.text: Good. Ask whether someone here repairs tiles.

originalDialogue.speaker: B
originalDialogue.text: Now we're at the moon landing.

originalDialogue.speaker: A
originalDialogue.text: Then put the original bucket under the original leak before it floats away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine, our house travels through time. Can we stop somewhere that fixes roof tiles?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ancient Rome. I'll find a roofer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Get a quote. The bucket's already half full.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I touched the dial. We're underwater now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. That same leak is admitting the sea. Reverse us while I empty the bucket into the sink.

bindings.scope: Fresh binding-only review of an explicit transfer-body amendment. Read the exact card, both original and accepted candidate single dialogues, and every original/proposed transfer field. Are the proposed fields faithful to the exact mechanism and their described source material? Identify real residual contradictions or unsupported details. Seed hashes still describe the historical originals; validated integration will bind the accepted dialogue only after your compatibility assessment. A compiled transfer is not an individually reviewed pair. Do not score single or pair dialogue; records must be empty. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
